name: light-tunnel

frames.best_why: Fully revealed tunnel with dense strands and bright comets sweeping in toward the centre.

tagline: White light strands swirl into a tunnel that drifts with the cursor.
summary: A full-screen swirl of curved light filaments converging into a dark vanishing point. The strands drift and carry racing comets, the centre bends toward the pointer, and a click sends a surge inward.
appearance: Hundreds of thin white strands curve inward like a whirlpool, brightest toward the outer edge and fading into a black hole at the centre. Short bright comets ride along some strands, giving the dark field a sense of speed.
behaviour: The whole swirl rotates and flexes slowly, bending its centre toward the pointer while streaks of light travel along the cables into the middle. Clicking sends a bright ring surging toward the vanishing point.
search_phrases: comets of light in a vortex
use_when: A hero or section needs a moving dark backdrop that reacts to the pointer without carrying any text.
avoid_when: A full-screen WebGL shader runs every frame, so it is heavy on phones and needs a sized parent.
customise: Colours, speed, flow direction, pulse speed, length, width and density, cable count, thickness, waviness, sway, bend, centre, glow, fades, grain, mouse strength, click surge and light mode are props.
weight_why: A full-screen fragment shader redraws every frame while the page is visible.

a11y.note: Decorative and aria-hidden; reduced motion freezes the drift and switches off pointer steering and click surges.

issues: Frame 1 catches the intro before the scene builds, so it looks nearly blank.
polish_why: Dense, convincing light strands; the intro leaves the first frame almost empty.
